# Jotter: the notyours demo app Jotter is a small notes app that notyours tests in the demo video. **These bugs are seeded and labelled on purpose.** Jotter contains three authorization mistakes of the kind coding agents often ship, so notyours has something real to find. Each one is marked in the code with a `// SEEDED BUG #n` comment and pinned by a test. Everything else is meant to be correct, including guest access. Don't copy this code into a real app, and don't expose it to a network. The server only listens on `127.0.0.1`. ## Run it ```bash node demo/server.js --seed # reset the database to the fixed seed, then serve http://127.0.0.1:3077 node demo/server.js # keep existing data (seeds automatically if the database is empty) node demo/server.js --seed-only # reset and exit ``` Options: `--port ` (default 3077, or `$PORT`) and `--db ` (default `demo/data/jotter.sqlite`, gitignored). The stack is Express 5, server-rendered HTML and sql.js (SQLite in WASM, no native modules). ## Seed Re-seeding always produces the same users, note ids and URLs, so cached (0-credit) Kane replays keep working. | User | Plan | Password (dev default) | Seeded data | |---|---|---|---| | `alice@jotter.test` | Pro | `alice-jotter-dev`, or `$JOTTER_ALICE_PW` | note **1001** "Travel documents": `Passport no. ` | | `bob@jotter.test` | Free | `bob-jotter-dev`, or `$JOTTER_BOB_PW` | note **1002** "Reminder": ``; his `/account` bio also shows `` | New sign-ups are free users, and their notes start at id 1003. **Canary tokens** are read from the first `identities.json` that exists: `$NOTYOURS_DIR/identities.json`, then `demo/.notyours/identities.json`, then `./.notyours/identities.json`. The file may be an `Identity[]` array or an object keyed by id. Only `token` is read, and invalid tokens are ignored. Without a file the fixed defaults are `NY-ALICE-JOTTERSEED2A` and `NY-BOB-JOTTERSEED2B`. Passwords come only from the environment variables above, set when you seed. Re-seed after changing tokens or passwords. ## Pages and API | Route | What it does | |---|---| | `/signup`, `/login`, `/logout` | Account basics (`/logout` takes GET or POST) | | `/notes` | Your own notes (correctly scoped) | | `/notes/new` | Write a note | | `/notes/:id` | View a note (**SEEDED BUG #1**) | | `/account` | Plan and profile bio, with bio editing (correctly scoped) | | `/pro/export` | Export page: Pro users see an "Export my notes" button, free users see an upsell | | `GET /api/notes/:id` | Note as JSON (**SEEDED BUG #2**) | | `POST /api/export` | Your notes as `jotter-export.txt`, or `jotter-export.csv` with `format=csv` (**SEEDED BUG #3**). Unknown formats get `400`. Other methods get `405` with `Allow: POST` | ## The seeded bugs | # | Where | Mistake | What a correct app does | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `routes/notes.js`, `GET /notes/:id` | Loads the note by id only, so any logged-in user can read anyone's note. | Adds `AND owner_id = ` and returns 404 | | 2 | `routes/notes.js`, `GET /api/notes/:id` | Returns the full record, including owner email and body, for any id. | Same owner check | | 3 | `routes/pro.js`, `POST /api/export` | The Pro gate is only a hidden button. The endpoint checks login, never the plan. | Returns 403 unless `plan = 'pro'` | **What stays correct (the controls):** guests get a redirect to `/login` from every page and a `401` from every API route. `/notes` and `/account` only show your own data. So the guest boundary holds, which shows that notyours doesn't cry wolf. ## notyours boundaries (`demo/.notyours/`) `config.yaml` sets `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:3077`. Paths in `surface` are relative to `demo/`. | File | Kind | Viewer → target | Expected on this app | |---|---|---|---| | `b1-cross-user.yaml` | cross-user | Bob → `/notes/1001`, `/api/notes/1001` | **LEAK** (bugs #1, #2) | | `b2-guest.yaml` | guest | logged out → same URLs | **HELD** | | `b3-plan-gate.yaml` | plan-gate | free Bob → `/pro/export`; `POST /api/export` | **LEAK** via the API (bug #3); the UI path holds | | `b4-sweep.yaml` | sweep | Bob → his own `/notes`, `/account` | **HELD** (Bob's token present, Alice's absent) | In B3, `targets.api` is written as `"POST "` because the export endpoint only accepts POST. A GET returns `405` (with `Allow: POST`), never a 404, so a wrong-method probe is visibly wrong and not a "denied". ## Tests ```bash npx vitest run --root demo ``` These are real HTTP requests against an in-memory database, with no Kane. They check that bugs #1–#3 are present, guests are blocked, positive controls work (owners see their own tokens), the happy paths work, and every boundary file parses with `BoundarySchema.strict()`. -rw-r--r-- 1 wheel 2159 18 Nov 19:18 test/boundaries.test.js -rw-r--r-- 1 wheel 14542 18 Nov 19:46 test/jotter.test.js test: total 40 drwxr-xr-x 4 wheel 128 18 Nov 19:46 . drwxr-xr-x 22 wheel 704 18 Nov 19:46 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 wheel 2159 18 Nov 19:18 boundaries.test.js -rw-r--r-- 1 wheel 14542 18 Nov 19:46 jotter.test.js // Demo-only test config: `npx vitest run --root demo`. import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'; export default defineConfig({ test: { include: ['test/**/*.test.js'], }, }); commit f1286db0b914b2bd4f1ad89f3f8f2cbe97420b96 Author: notyours-loop Date: Wed Nov 18 19:55:19 2026 +0500 setup loop-run-3: restore seeded bugs #1/#2 (human) diff --git a/routes/notes.js b/routes/notes.js index bb4be17..9f43349 100644 --- a/routes/notes.js +++ b/routes/notes.js @@ -1,7 +1,8 @@ // /notes, /notes/new, /notes/:id and GET /api/notes/:id // -// SEEDED BUG #1 and #2 (see demo/README.md) are fixed here: every lookup by note id is also -// scoped to the logged-in owner, so another user's note id is a 404. +// Contains SEEDED BUG #1 and #2 on purpose (see demo/README.md). They are the kind of +// authorization mistake coding agents often ship: the route checks that you are logged in, +// but never checks that the note is yours. import { Router } from 'express'; import { requireLogin, requireLoginApi } from '../session.js'; import { errorBox, esc, formatDate, page } from '../views.js'; @@ -61,16 +62,12 @@ export function notesRoutes(db) { r.get('/notes/:id', requireLogin, (req, res) => { const id = parseId(req.params.id); - // Owner-scoped: someone else's note id is a 404, the same as a missing one (was SEEDED BUG #1). - const note = id === null ? undefined : db.get(`${NOTE_SELECT} WHERE n.id = ?
